result.note: Tested the start year of Delhi's petrol vehicle ban and its first-in-India status, both stated in the story.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, Delhi announced an electric-vehicle policy with an outlay of INR 150 billion. Consider the following statements about it:
items: The ban on registering new petrol three-wheelers and light trucks takes effect from 2030.
Delhi became the first Indian city to bar new combustion-engine registrations in any vehicle category.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: The ban on new petrol three-wheelers and light trucks applies from 2027, not 2030. It comes under an INR 150 billion (USD 1.59 billion) electric-vehicle policy and makes Delhi the first Indian city to bar new combustion-engine registrations in any category.
questions.source: Delhi banned new petrol three-wheelers and light trucks from 2027 under a INR 150 billion (USD 1.59 billion) electric-vehicle policy, the first Indian city to bar new combustion-engine registrations in any category.
